regime_context: Detector shows broad, mild rotation with Gold Miners as a durable, uncrowded, high-breadth leader (rank 1, hurst trend, breadth 1.0), silver/copper metals clustered just behind, and no one-narrative dominance. The only validated edge is drawdown/shake-out control via the absolute-trend gate, which is active (gate_helps true); momentum rank is a focus lens only.
emerging_watch: Watch whether Telecom (rank 13, ineligible, crowding_z -1.41) or Utilities & Renewables (rank 11, mean-revert) start to confirm a leadership handoff: the observable to retire this watch is either of those themes entering the top-5 ranks AND clearing the trend-gate eligibility for 10 consecutive trading days. Until then, no confirmed rotation exists.

theses.subject: Gold Miners
theses.thesis: Gold Miners hold the lead with high durability (0.85), broad strength (breadth 1.0), and an intact trend tag. The trend-gate discipline supports staying with the strongest, most cohesive theme rather than reaching down the ranks; crowding is absent so no sizing caution applies. This is a continuation lean on the existing leader, not a rank-derived return forecast.
theses.dissent: A sharp reversal in gold itself (not miners) could unwind the leadership even though momentum is high right now, and the rank-IC on momentum is essentially zero historically.

falsifier.text: XGD.TO falls below the S&P/TSX by 8% before the check-by date

theses.subject: Silver & Royalties
theses.thesis: Silver & Royalties sits directly behind gold with broad strength (breadth 1.0) and a mixed-but-positive durability tag. This reads as a correlated precious-metals leg rather than an independent narrative; leaning with the cluster rather than reaching across sectors keeps the call within the dominant regime structure.
theses.dissent: Silver is more industrially exposed than gold, so a commodity-buying pullback hits it harder while the detector still shows it as a top-ranked theme.

falsifier.text: Silver & Royalties lags Gold Miners by 6% before the check-by date

theses.subject: Base Metals & Copper
theses.thesis: Base Metals & Copper is crowded (crowding_z 1.23, crowded true). Guardrails explicitly forbid fading on crowding, so this is not a short or fade; 'avoid' reflects a size-down/skip stance because the crowding flag removes the case for initiating or adding here while the trend is unproven (hurst mixed).
theses.dissent: Copper could continue its run driven by macro reflation; crowding alone has no forward basket-level timing edge, so avoiding may simply mean missing continuation.

falsifier.text: XBM.TO outperforms Gold Miners by 5% before the check-by date

macro_narrative.note: market-level macro/policy/geo narrative flow; coincident, not per-theme, never a trigger
